question: Would you go?

beats.text: A governor asked her to cross the ocean and teach.
In 1642, she first heard of Ville-Marie, a new colony in Canada.
beats.scene: A bare seventeenth-century French room at night: a large hand-drawn map of the New World unrolled on a plain wooden table, curling at the edges, one candle burning beside it, a hard shaft of light across the vast empty ocean on the map, deep shadows. Skewed angular painted-set walls. No people.

beats.text: About ten years later, she met its governor, Maisonneuve.
He was looking for someone to teach the colony's children.
beats.scene: A small seventeenth-century wooden fort-town on a wide river island at dusk: a log palisade, a few steep-roofed log houses, a single small cross, vast dark forest and mist beyond, hard low light from one side. Skewed angular painted-set architecture. No people.

beats.text: She later told of a prayer, in which Our Lady said: Go, I will not forsake you.

beats.scene: An old walled seventeenth-century French town gate at dawn seen from outside, a bare road leading away from it between bare fields into mist, a hard low light from the side, long shadows, crooked half-timbered roofs behind the wall. Skewed angular painted-set architecture. No people.

beats.text: She was thirty-three, and the road led to the sea.

next_voice: Next, in Part Three: the crossing.
